central_unknown: McLaren's form appears to have dropped significantly compared to earlier in the season, with ML projecting Norris at only P6 (exp 15.6 pts) and Piastri P7 (exp 17.4 pts). The key uncertainty is whether Mercedes and Ferrari maintain their recent dominance at COTA, and whether Verstappen can convert his ML-projected P1 finish into a big captain haul.

budget_tiers.fills: Hadjar or Hulkenberg as budget driver
Lindblad or Hulkenberg as budget filler

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: ML projects 26.1 exp pts (proj 39.3), ppm 1.81, MEDIUM risk, predicted quali P3 → finish P1 with a 90% CI of [-11.0, 51.0]. Verstappen is the clear #1 ML captain pick. Channel consensus from prior weeks consistently backs Verstappen as the premier captain on non-sprint weekends where he's expected to win. His driver-of-the-day potential (7 awards this season) adds upside not fully captured in projections.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Charles Leclerc
captains.reason: ML projects 22.4 exp pts (proj 27.4), ppm 1.33, value 0.93, MEDIUM risk. Leclerc predicted quali P2 → finish P3. Multiple channels noted Leclerc has been 'on the trend up' and Ferrari's race pace has been strong. At 24.1M he offers better value than the Mercedes drivers and could challenge for podium. If Verstappen DNFs (14% probability), Leclerc could be the top scorer.

buy.name: Isack Hadjar
buy.note: ML projects 8.9 exp pts, ppm 1.21, predicted P8 finish. Excellent budget enabler with solid floor — channels consistently recommend him as a must-have stopgap between A-tier and B-tier drivers. Strong price rise candidate at this level.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: At or near price floor — cannot lose value. In 96%+ of top 500 teams per channel consensus. Budget anchor that frees capital for premium drivers. Audi ML exp 14.2 pts as constructor suggests he contributes meaningfully.

buy.name: Arvid Lindblad
buy.note: Channels consistently list him as a no-brainer budget pick with overtake upside from lower grid positions. Pairs well with Hadjar for Racing Bulls constructor coverage if needed.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Channel favorite as differential — less than 5% ownership in top 500. Last five races: 12, 25, 16, 3, 17 pts. Channels note he 'proves time and again he is capable of delivering a stunning performance.' COTA may not be his strongest track but price rise potential is real.

consider.name: Fernando Alonso
consider.note: Channels flag him as underrated differential (<1% ownership) who performs well at low-speed corner tracks. However COTA is more power-dependent than Singapore/Hungary — channels themselves note 'COTA probably won't be an ideal option' for Alonso. Risky pick.

consider.name: Sergio Perez
consider.note: Channel identifies as transfer target/trap — cheap at 3M but DNF-prone. In 27% of top 500 teams. Useful if building a mega-team with Verstappen + Red Bull constructor, but instability is a real concern. Channel warns 'have a plan to get him out as soon as possible.'

avoid: Carlos Sainz — channels note poor performance and high price (~13M) is unjustified
Valtteri Bottas — reliability issues, channels warn 'reliability is just not there' with frequent DNFs causing massive negative scores
Alex Albon — channels say 'not going to touch him with a 20-ft pole' due to Williams underperformance

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: No channel discussion suggests COTA as a wildcard weekend. The non-sprint format reduces the urgency. Save for a higher-value weekend where constructors shift or multiple penalties create unusual opportunities.

chips.name: 3x Boost
chips.reason: Channels used 3x at Monza on Antonelli to strong effect. ML projects Verstappen at 39.3 proj pts — a 3x captain on Verstappen could yield ~78+ pts. However, his 14% DNF risk and MEDIUM rating suggest waiting for a lower-risk weekend may be prudent. If you have strong conviction in Mercedes dominance, Antonelli 3x (LOW risk, 4% DNF) is safer but lower ceiling.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: Channel analysis from prior races showed limitless can score lower than 3x boost in certain configurations. Non-sprint weekend reduces the total points available. Save for a sprint weekend or a round with clear constructor reshuffling needs.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: Useful if qualifying reshuffles the grid unexpectedly. Channels routinely mention keeping final fix flexibility for post-qualifying swaps — particularly relevant if Antonelli (predicted P1 quali) or Verstappen underperform in qualifying.

watch_items: Mercedes aero package split: Russell ran older spec winning in Baku while Antonelli had the Malaysia package — watch which spec each runs at COTA and whether the Malaysia upgrade performs better on smoother tarmac

George Russell second engine penalty: channels confirm he'll likely need another penalty later this season since current PUs won't last 7 races — could create overtake-points opportunity in a future race
McLaren decline: ML projects both Norris (exp 15.6) and Piastri (exp 17.4) significantly below Mercedes and Ferrari drivers — monitor FP sessions to see if this is a real regression or track-specific
Verstappen DNF risk: ML flags 14% DNF probability and MEDIUM risk — watch for any mechanical concerns in practice
Antonelli qualifying form: ML predicts P1 in qualifying but only P4 finish — monitor whether he can convert front-row starts into race results or continues to fade
Red Bull constructor value at 32.7M: ML projects 46.6 exp pts vs McLaren's 44.3 at 32.4M — if Verstappen wins and Lawson scores, Red Bull constructor could outperform McLaren
arc: The United States GP marks a potential inflection point in the constructor hierarchy. Mercedes and Ferrari appear to have separated from McLaren in the ML projections, which could reshape F1 Fantasy team structures for the remaining races. Verstappen's strong COTA projection (P1 finish) reinforces his captain credentials heading into Mexico (Round 21) — a track that has historically favored Red Bull. The budget-building phase appears to be stabilizing, with most B-tier drivers approaching optimal price points. If McLaren's decline holds through Austin, managers should pivot away from McLaren constructor for Mexico and consider Red Bull or Racing Bulls as the second constructor alongside Mercedes or Ferrari. Russell's pending second engine penalty could create a high-value overtake opportunity at an upcoming race — keep transfers flexible to capitalize.
